14	# Plan: Multiple chat tabs with a mode and a subject, and buttons that open interviews
15	
16	Concept: [OKR Viewer - Product Vision](../../Concepts/OKR%20Viewer%20-%20Product%20Vision.md)
17	(vocabulary: Tab, Interview) and [Teams as Agents - Design](../../Concepts/Teams%20as%20Agents%20-%20Design.md)
18	(interviews are the on-ramp to personas).
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	There is one conversation: `messages` at `web/src/App.svelte:25`, rendered by
23	`web/src/Chat.svelte`, with history sliced to the last ten turns at `App.svelte:32-35`.
24	Buttons on a node or a team want to open a focused conversation about that one thing without
25	polluting the general chat, and an interview needs a different prompt: ask, don't answer.
26	
27	## Goal
28	
29	The chat panel has tabs; each tab has a mode (`free`, `interview-node`, `interview-team`,
30	`interview-new`) and a subject; interview tabs open with the assistant's first question and end
31	by proposing Actions that go through `commit()`.
32	
33	## Decisions (locked in)
34	
35	1. **Tab shape:** `{ id, title, mode, subject, messages, loading }` where `subject` is
36	   `{ kind: 'node', id } | { kind: 'team', id } | { kind: 'new', parentId: string | null } | null`.
37	   `chats = $state([])`, `activeChatId = $state()`. Undo stack, highlight and selection stay
38	   global: there is one scene.
39	2. **Kick-off turn.** Opening an interview tab sends a synthetic user turn
40	   `"Begin the interview."` flagged `hidden: true` so the UI does not render it, but it is kept
41	   in history so the API sees strict user/assistant alternation
42	   (`service/validate.js:17-24` drops leading assistant turns). (Interview answer: agent asks
43	   first.)
44	3. **Request gains `mode` and `subject`**, additive. The response shape and the `respond` tool
45	   do not change; proposed edits come back as `actions` and are committed like any other.
46	4. **Interview rules in the prompt:** one question per turn; at most eight questions; reflect
47	   what you heard in one sentence before asking the next; when you have enough, summarise and
48	   return `actions`; `highlight` the subject's nodes on every turn. `interview-new` ends with
49	   `add` under `subject.parentId`; if `parentId` is null, the first question is which objective
50	   the new node supports. `interview-team` may end with `editUnit` (charter changes) and node
51	   edits for the team's nodes.
52	5. **Free tabs use the current prompt unchanged.** Mode only adds a section.
53	6. **In memory only.** Tabs vanish on reload, like everything else.
54	7. **Per-tab loading.** Two tabs may have requests in flight; each response lands in the tab
55	   that sent it, matched by tab id captured at send time.
56	
57	## Phase 1 — Schema
58	
59	1. `schema/src/chat-request.schema.json`: add `mode` (enum of the four, default `free` in
60	   description) and `subject` (`oneOf` the three shapes, or null). Fixtures:
61	   `valid/chat-request.interview-node.json`, `valid/chat-request.interview-new-no-parent.json`,
62	   `invalid/chat-request.bad-mode.json`.
63	2. `schema/index.d.ts`: export `ChatMode`, `ChatSubject`. Rebuild.
64	
65	## Phase 2 — Web state
66	
67	1. `App.svelte:25-26`: replace `messages` / `loading` with `chats` and `activeChatId`
68	   (Decision 1). `const activeChat = $derived(chats.find(c => c.id === activeChatId))`.
69	2. `send(chatId, message, { hidden = false } = {})`: look up the chat; build `history` from
70	   its `messages` (same filter/slice as `:32-35`, including hidden turns); push the user turn
71	   with `hidden`; set `chat.loading = true`; POST with `mode`, `subject`, `context` (from
72	   `CHAT_CONTEXT`); on response `commit()` actions, set global `highlight`, push the assistant
73	   turn into that chat. Errors as today (`:63-65`).
74	3. `newChat({ mode, subject, title })`: creates the tab, makes it active, and for interview
75	   modes calls `send(id, 'Begin the interview.', { hidden: true })`. Returns the id.
76	   `closeChat(id)`: remove; if it was active, activate the previous tab; never close the last
77	   tab (create a fresh free one instead).
78	4. Boot: one free tab titled "Chat".
79	5. `recall(ids)` (`:135-137`) unchanged.
80	
81	## Phase 3 — Chat.svelte
82	
83	1. Props: `chats`, `activeChatId`, `onSelectChat`, `onCloseChat`, `onNewChat`, `onSend`,
84	   `onRecall`.
85	2. Tab bar above `.messages` (`Chat.svelte:33`): one button per tab (title truncated to 24
86	   chars with the full title in `title`), an `×` on each tab except when only one exists, a
87	   `+` that opens a small menu: "New chat", "Interview me about a new OKR".
88	3. Render `activeChat.messages`, skipping `hidden` turns. Suggestions chips (`:7-11`, `:34-41`)
89	   only in free tabs' empty state; interview tabs show a one-line hint ("The assistant asks,
90	   you answer. Say 'that's enough' to wrap up.") while the kick-off is loading.
91	4. Loading indicator (`:59-61`) and disabled input (`:69-71`) keyed on `activeChat.loading`.
92	5. Assistant turns that carried actions already show an "N edits" pill (`:47-49`); in
93	   interview tabs also show "Undo" next to it, calling the global undo.
94	
95	## Phase 4 — Launchers
96	
97	1. `Detail.svelte` header: "Interview me about this OKR" →
98	   `onNewChat({ mode: 'interview-node', subject: { kind: 'node', id }, title: 'Interview: <label>' })`.
99	   In edit mode on an objective or the root, also "Interview me about a new KR here" →
100	   `interview-new` with `parentId = node.id`.
101	2. `TeamEditor.svelte` header: "Interview me about this team" → `interview-team`, title
102	   `Team: <name>`.
103	3. Chat `+` menu: "Interview me about a new OKR" → `interview-new` with
104	   `parentId = selected node if its level is objective or company, else null`.
105	4. `App.svelte`: pass `onNewChat={newChat}` to the panels.
106	
107	## Phase 5 — Service
108	
109	1. `service/index.js:24`: destructure `mode = 'free'`, `subject = null`; validate the subject
110	   id against the tree or `company.units`; an unknown subject downgrades the mode to `free`
111	   with a log line rather than a 400.
112	2. `service/prompt.js`: `systemPrompt(tree, company, selectedNodeId, context, { mode, subject })`.
113	   Add a `## Your role in this conversation` section per mode:
114	   - `interview-node`: "You are interviewing the user about <label> (<level>, owned by <team>).
115	     Goal: make it an outcome with a metric and a target, and confirm it supports <parent
116	     label>." plus Decision 4 rules.
117	   - `interview-team`: "You are interviewing the user about the <name> team. Goal: fill or
118	     sharpen its charter (mission, process, what it owns, what it depends on) and check its
119	     objectives fit." Render the current charter so the model asks about gaps, not what it
120	     already has.
121	   - `interview-new`: "You are helping the user define a new OKR under <parent label>" (or the
122	     ask-for-parent variant).
123	   - `free`: nothing added.
124	3. `[chat]` log line: append `· mode=<mode>`.
125	
126	## Phase 6 — Styles
127	
128	`web/src/app.css` chat block (`:118-150`): `.tabs` row with overflow-x scroll, active tab
129	border in `var(--accent)`, `.tab .close`, the `+` menu as a small absolute popover.
130	
131	## Verification
132	
133	- Boot: one "Chat" tab; the demo script runs unchanged in it.
134	- Select `kr-7`, click "Interview me about this OKR": a new tab opens, the assistant asks a
135	  question within ~3 s, `kr-7` pulses, the kick-off turn is not visible. Answer four or five
136	  questions; the assistant summarises and returns an `edit`; `kr-7` has a metric and target;
137	  Undo reverts it; the free tab's messages are untouched.
138	- Open Marketing's editor, "Interview me about this team": questions target charter gaps; the
139	  end result is an `editUnit` with `charter` fields; the TeamEditor shows them.
140	- `+` → "Interview me about a new OKR" with `obj-3` selected: the first question is about the
141	  KR, not the parent. With nothing selected: the first question asks which objective.
142	- Send in tab A, switch to tab B and send there before A returns: both replies land in the
143	  right tabs; the scene highlights the most recent reply.
144	- Close a tab: the previous tab activates; closing the last tab yields a fresh "Chat".
145	- Service: `mode: "interview-node"` with an unknown subject id → 200, log shows the downgrade.
146	
147	## Out of scope
148	
149	- Persisting tabs. Renaming tabs. Drag-reordering.
150	- Persona, review and debate modes (`Teams as Agents - Design`; future
151	  `TEAM_AGENT_DISCUSSIONS.md`). This plan leaves `mode` as an enum so those are additive.
152	- Streaming.
153	- An "end interview" button; "that's enough" in text is sufficient for v1.
154	
155	## Risks / rollback
156	
157	- The kick-off turn is visible to the model as literal user text; if replies start with "Sure,
158	  I'll begin the interview" the prompt should say the phrase is a system signal to ignore.
159	- History cap: `App.svelte:34` sends the last ten turns. An eight-question interview is 16+
160	  turns, so the summary turn may not see the first answers. Raise the cap to 24 for interview
161	  tabs (schema allows 50) and keep 10 for free tabs.
162	- Rollback: `chats` is a superset of `messages`; reverting to a single array is mechanical.

225	  async function send(message) {

254	      // crosses before it reaches the renderer — so check it here too, and
255	      // refuse to apply anything from a response we do not recognise.

257	      if (!checked.ok) {
258	        throw new Error(`the service sent a response this app can't read (${checked.errors.slice(0, 3).join('; ')})`);
259	      }
260	      const { reply, actions, highlight: ids } = checked.value;
261	      if (actions.length) commit(actions, { actor: 'assistant', reason: reply });
262	      highlight = ids;
263	      messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: reply, highlight: ids, actions: actions.length });
264	    } catch (err) {
265	      messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: `Something went wrong: ${err.message}`, error: true });
266	    } finally {
267	      loading = false;
268	    }
269	  }

271	  function undo() {
272	    if (!undoStack.length) return;
273	    const previous = undoStack[undoStack.length - 1];
274	    tree = previous.tree;
275	    company = previous.company;
276	    datasetId = previous.datasetId;
277	    history = previous.history; // a true revert: the change entry goes with the change
278	    undoStack = undoStack.slice(0, -1);
279	    highlight = [];
280	    messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: 'Reverted the last change.', note: true });
281	  }
282	
283	  // Reset, import and dataset switch all replace the document, so they replace
284	  // both halves of it: a tree from one dataset beside another's org would leave
285	  // every unitId dangling.
286	  function reset() {
287	    undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()];
288	    tree = structuredClone(getDataset(datasetId).document.tree);
289	    company = companyOf(datasetId);
290	    history = historyOf(datasetId); // back to the dataset's own history, not ours
291	    highlight = [];
292	    selectedId = null;
293	    editing = false;
294	    panel = null;
295	  }
296	
297	  // Switching datasets is the same snapshot-then-replace as import: undoable,
298	  // and it says in the chat what just landed.
299	  function switchDataset(id) {
300	    if (id === datasetId) return;
301	    const dataset = getDataset(id);
302	    undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()];
303	    datasetId = dataset.id;
304	    tree = structuredClone(dataset.document.tree);
305	    company = companyOf(dataset.id);
306	    history = historyOf(dataset.id);
307	    highlight = [];
308	    selectedId = null;
309	    editing = false;
310	    panel = null;
311	    messages.push({
312	      role: 'assistant',
313	      content: `Loaded "${dataset.title}" (${tree.nodes.length} nodes). Undo to go back.`,
314	      note: true
315	    });
316	  }
317	
318	  // ── export / import ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
319	  //
320	  // The file is an OkrDocument: the tree plus a schemaVersion the reader checks
321	  // before it trusts anything inside. Same package on both sides, so a file
322	  // written here is a file the service would accept.
323	
324	  let fileInput;
325	
326	  function exportTree() {
327	    const doc = createDocument({ tree, company, history, meta: { title: getDataset(datasetId).title } });
328	    const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }));
329	    const a = document.createElement('a');
330	    a.href = url;
331	    a.download = `okr-${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.json`;
332	    a.click();
333	    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
334	    messages.push({ role: 'assistant', content: `Exported ${tree.nodes.length} nodes to ${a.download}.`, note: true });
335	  }
336	
337	  async function importTree(e) {
338	    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
339	    e.target.value = ''; // so re-picking the same file fires change again
340	    if (!file) return;
341	
342	    const out = parseDocument(await file.text());
343	    if (!out.ok) {
344	      messages.push({
345	        role: 'assistant',
346	        content: `Couldn't import ${file.name}: ${out.errors.slice(0, 3).join('; ')}`,
347	        error: true
348	      });
349	      return;
350	    }
351	
352	    undoStack = [...undoStack, snapshot()]; // same snapshot-then-replace as reset()
353	    tree = out.document.tree;
354	    // A file written before teams existed has no `company`; it gets an empty
355	    // org named after the file rather than keeping ours, which would claim
356	    // teams the imported tree never referenced. Its `owner` text still shows.
357	    company = structuredClone(out.document.company ?? { name: out.document.meta?.title ?? file.name, units: [] });
358	    history = structuredClone(out.document.history ?? emptyHistory());
359	    highlight = [];
360	    selectedId = null;
361	    editing = false;
362	    panel = null;
363	    // The snapshot above already covers the import, so this commit only writes
364	    // the boundary marker: an empty batch saying where the file came from.
365	    commit([], { actor: 'import', reason: `Imported ${file.name}`, undoable: false });
366	    const warned = out.warnings.length ? ` ${out.warnings.length} warning${out.warnings.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}: ${out.warnings.slice(0, 3).join('; ')}` : '';
367	    messages.push({
368	      role: 'assistant',
369	      content: `Imported ${tree.nodes.length} nodes from ${file.name}. Undo to go back.${warned}`,
370	      note: true
371	    });
372	  }
373	
374	  // `keepEditing` is for the Detail panel's "add a child": the new node is

377	  function select(id, keepEditing = false) {

382	    panel = id ? { kind: 'node' } : null;
383	    if (highlight.length) highlight = []; // a user selection supersedes the assistant's pointer
384	  }
385	
386	  // ── teams ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
387	
388	  function showTeams() {
389	    panel = { kind: 'teams' };
390	    selectedId = null;
391	    editing = false;
392	  }
393	
394	  function openTeam(id) {
395	    panel = { kind: 'team', id };
396	    selectedId = null;
397	    editing = false;
398	  }
399	
400	  // apply.js turns an addUnit with an id that already exists into an editUnit,
401	  // so the id has to be new. Slugged from the name, because a unit id is read
402	  // by the model in charters and in `dependsOn`.
403	  function freshUnitId(name) {
404	    const base = name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-|-$/g, '').slice(0, 40) || 'team';
405	    if (!company.units.some((u) => u.id === base)) return base;
406	    for (let i = 2; i < 100; i++) if (!company.units.some((u) => u.id === `${base}-${i}`)) return `${base}-${i}`;
407	    return `${base}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;
408	  }
409	
410	  function recall(ids) {
411	    highlight = [...ids]; // new array so the graph effect re-runs
412	  }
413	
414	  function onKey(e) {
415	    const tag = e.target?.tagName;
416	    if (tag === 'INPUT' || tag === 'TEXTAREA' || tag === 'SELECT') return;
417	    if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === 'z') {

424	<svelte:window onkeydown={onKey} />

469	          }}

480	          onAdd={() => {

482	            commit([action], { actor: 'user', reason: describe(action) });

486	      {:else if panel?.kind === 'team' && selectedUnit}

493	          onFocusField={focusField}

140	## How to respond
141	- \`reply\`: 1–3 conversational sentences. Refer to nodes by their label, never by id. No JSON, no bullet lists.
142	- \`highlight\`: the ids of every node your reply talks about. Be generous — the camera flies to these and they pulse, which is how the user follows along. Include the parent when the relationship matters. Only use ids that exist in the tree, or that you are adding in this same response.
143	- \`actions\`: only when the user asks for a change (rewrite, fix, move, add, remove, make measurable, tighten, etc.). Send an empty array for questions.
144	
145	## Actions
146	- { "op": "edit", "id", "fields": { label?, owner?, unitId?, metric?, target?, contributes? } } — rewriting a KR to be measurable means a label that states the outcome, a concrete \`metric\`, and a \`target\` with a baseline and a goal (e.g. "31% → 50% by Q4"). Raise \`contributes\` when the fix actually makes it support its parent. To change who owns a node, set \`unitId\` to a team id from \`<teams>\` (or null for none) and do not set \`owner\`.
147	- { "op": "relink", "id", "fields": { "parent" } } — move a node under a different parent. Follow it with an edit that updates \`contributes\` for the new fit.
148	- { "op": "add", "id", "fields": { level, parent, label, unitId, metric, target, contributes } } — new ids must be unique and of the form "kr-<short-slug>" or "obj-<short-slug>".
149	- { "op": "delete", "id" } — removes the node and everything under it. Only when explicitly asked.
150	- { "op": "editUnit", "id", "fields": { name?, parent?, charter? } } — change a team. \`charter\` is merged one field at a time, so send only the fields you are changing. Only write a charter when the user has told you something about how the team actually works; do not invent a mission for a team they merely named.
151	- { "op": "addUnit", "id", "fields": { name, parent?, charter? } } — a team that is not in \`<teams>\` yet. Ids are slugs of the name, e.g. "field-marketing".
152	- { "op": "deleteUnit", "id" } — removes a team. Nothing is deleted from the tree: its nodes keep their \`owner\` text and lose their \`unitId\`, and teams under it move up. Only when explicitly asked.
153	- Never invent ids. Never change a node's level. Never touch the company objective unless asked.
154	- When you edit, say what changed and why in plain language.
155	
156	Be direct and specific. A good OKR coach names the problem ("this is an activity, not an outcome") and proposes the fix.
157	
158	${viewBlock(tree, company, selectedNodeId, context)}`;
159	}

2	import express from 'express';

7	
8	const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT) || 8787;

10	app.use(express.json({ limit: '2mb' }));
11	
12	// Created lazily so a missing key surfaces as a clear 500, not a crash at boot.
13	let client;
14	const getClient = () => (client ??= new Anthropic());
15	
16	app.get('/api/health', (_req, res) => res.json({ ok: true, model: MODEL }));
17	
18	app.post('/api/chat', async (req, res) => {
19	  // One structural check for the whole body, straight from the shared schema.
20	  const request = validateChatRequest(req.body);
21	  if (!request.ok) {
22	    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'The request does not match the chat schema.', details: request.errors });
23	  }
24	  const { tree, company = null, message, selectedNodeId = null, history = [], context = null } = request.value;
25	
26	  // Shape is not enough: a tree can be well-formed and still be unusable.
27	  // Warnings (an off-ladder link, say) are normal mid-edit, so they only log.
28	  const semantics = checkTreeSemantics(tree);
29	  if (semantics.errors.length) {
30	    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'The tree is structurally broken.', details: semantics.errors });
31	  }
32	  if (semantics.warnings.length) console.warn('[chat] tree warnings:', JSON.stringify(semantics.warnings));
33	
34	  // The org gets the same treatment, and only when it is sent at all: a request
35	  // without `company` is a document that has no teams, not a broken one.
36	  if (company) {
37	    const org = checkCompanySemantics(company);
38	    if (org.errors.length) {
39	      return res.status(400).json({ error: 'The company is structurally broken.', details: org.errors });
40	    }
41	    if (org.warnings.length) console.warn('[chat] company warnings:', JSON.stringify(org.warnings));
42	  }
43	  // A node pointing at a team that is gone is never fatal — it just means the
44	  // model should read that node's `owner` text instead.
45	  const ownership = checkOwnership(tree, company);
46	  if (ownership.warnings.length) console.warn('[chat] ownership warnings:', JSON.stringify(ownership.warnings));
47	
48	  const selected = typeof selectedNodeId === 'string' && tree.nodes.some((n) => n.id === selectedNodeId) ? selectedNodeId : null;
49	  // Same treatment for what the user is looking at: unknown ids are dropped,
50	  // never rejected. A stale highlight is not a broken request.
51	  const view = sanitizeContext(tree, company, context);
52	  if (view.dropped.length) console.warn('[chat] context: dropped', JSON.stringify(view.dropped));
53	  const messages = mergeTurns([...sanitizeHistory(history), { role: 'user', content: message.trim() }]);
54	
55	  const started = Date.now();
56	  try {
57	    const response = await getClient().messages.create({
58	      model: MODEL,
59	      max_tokens: 4096,
60	      system: systemPrompt(tree, company, selected, view.context),
61	      tools: [RESPOND_TOOL],
62	      tool_choice: { type: 'tool', name: 'respond' },
63	      messages
64	    });
65	
66	    const call = response.content.find((b) => b.type === 'tool_use' && b.name === 'respond');
67	    if (!call) {
68	      const text = response.content.filter((b) => b.type === 'text').map((b) => b.text).join('\n').trim();
69	      const why = response.stop_reason === 'refusal' ? 'declined to answer' : `stopped early (${response.stop_reason})`;
70	      console.warn(`[chat] no respond call: ${why}`);
71	      return res.json({ reply: text || `The model ${why}. Try rephrasing.`, actions: [], highlight: [] });
72	    }
73	
74	    const out = validateResponse(tree, company, call.input);
75	    if (out.dropped.length) console.warn('[chat] dropped from model output:', JSON.stringify(out.dropped));
76	    // `ctx=` says what the user was looking at, because a reply that resolved
77	    // "this" to the wrong thing is a prompt bug you cannot see from the reply.
78	    const p = view.context?.panel;
79	    const ctx = p ? `${p.kind}${p.id ? `:${p.id}` : ''}${p.field ? `/${p.field}` : ''}` : 'none';
80	    console.log(
81	      `[chat] ${Date.now() - started}ms · ${response.usage.input_tokens}in/${response.usage.output_tokens}out · ${out.actions.length} actions · ${out.highlight.length} highlights · ctx=${ctx}`
82	    );
83	    res.json({ reply: out.reply, actions: out.actions, highlight: out.highlight });
84	  } catch (err) {
85	    // The SDK throws a plain Error (not AuthenticationError) when it finds no
86	    // credentials at all, so match that case explicitly.
87	    if (err instanceof Anthropic.AuthenticationError || /authentication method/i.test(err?.message ?? '')) {
88	      console.error('[chat] auth failed — is ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set in service/.env?');
89	      return res.status(500).json({ error: 'The service has no valid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.' });
90	    }
91	    if (err instanceof Anthropic.RateLimitError) {
92	      return res.status(429).json({ error: 'Rate limited by the Claude API. Wait a moment and retry.' });
93	    }
94	    if (err instanceof Anthropic.APIConnectionError) {
95	      console.error('[chat] connection error:', err.message);
96	      return res.status(502).json({ error: 'Could not reach the Claude API.' });
97	    }
98	    if (err instanceof Anthropic.APIError) {
99	      console.error(`[chat] API error ${err.status}:`, err.message);
100	      return res.status(502).json({ error: `Claude API error (${err.status}).` });
101	    }
102	    console.error('[chat] unexpected error:', err);
103	    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Unexpected server error.' });
104	  }
105	});

1	// Claude will occasionally invent node IDs. Everything it sends back is
2	// filtered against the tree the browser sent us, so nothing unknown reaches
3	// the renderer.
4	//
5	// Two layers, and the split matters:
6	//
7	//   @okr-viewer/schema's validateAction()  — shape. Is this an action at all?
8	//   the checks below                       — reference. Does it fit *this* tree?
9	//
10	// Shape lives in the package because the browser needs the same answer. The
11	// referential checks are tree-relative and stay here.
12	
13	import { validateAction } from '@okr-viewer/schema';
14	
15	// Keep only well-formed turns, cap the length, and merge consecutive
16	// same-role turns so the API always sees strict user/assistant alternation.
17	export function sanitizeHistory(history, maxTurns = 12) {
18	  const turns = (Array.isArray(history) ? history : [])
19	    .filter((m) => m && (m.role === 'user' || m.role === 'assistant') && typeof m.content === 'string' && m.content.trim())
20	    .slice(-maxTurns)

26	export function mergeTurns(turns) {
27	  const out = [];
28	  for (const t of turns) {
29	    const last = out[out.length - 1];
30	    if (last && last.role === t.role) last.content += '\n\n' + t.content;
31	    else out.push({ ...t });
32	  }
33	  return out;

36	// The browser's view context, filtered against the document it came with.
37	//
38	// Context is advisory: it says what the user is looking at, and being wrong
39	// about that is never worth a 400. A panel pointed at a node or team that this
40	// tree does not have names nothing, so the whole panel goes; highlights are
41	// filtered one by one. Everything dropped is reported so the caller can log
42	// it — a context that keeps arriving broken is a client bug worth seeing.
43	export function sanitizeContext(tree, company, context) {
44	  const dropped = [];
45	  if (!context || typeof context !== 'object') return { context: null, dropped };
46	
47	  const known = new Set(tree.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
48	  const knownUnits = new Set((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => u.id));
49	
50	  let panel = null;
51	  if (context.panel) {
52	    const { kind, id = null, editing, field } = context.panel;
53	    const needed = kind === 'node' ? known : kind === 'team' ? knownUnits : null;
54	    if (needed && !(typeof id === 'string' && needed.has(id))) {
55	      dropped.push(`panel ${kind}:${id ?? 'none'}`);
56	    } else {
57	      panel = { kind };
58	      if (id != null) panel.id = id;
59	      if (typeof editing === 'boolean') panel.editing = editing;
60	      if (field) panel.field = field;
61	    }
62	  }
63	
64	  const wanted = Array.isArray(context.highlighted) ? context.highlighted : [];
65	  const highlighted = wanted.filter((id) => known.has(id));
66	  if (highlighted.length !== wanted.length) {
67	    dropped.push(`highlighted ${wanted.filter((id) => !known.has(id)).join(', ')}`);
68	  }
69	
70	  const dataset = typeof context.dataset === 'string' ? context.dataset.trim() : '';
71	  return { context: { panel, highlighted, ...(dataset ? { dataset } : {}) }, dropped };
72	}

74	export function validateResponse(tree, company, input) {
75	  const known = new Set(tree.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
76	  const parentOf = new Map(tree.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n.parent]));
77	  // Teams are filtered exactly like nodes, and against the same moving target:
78	  // an addUnit earlier in the batch makes its id usable by a later action.
79	  const knownUnits = new Set((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => u.id));
80	  const unitParentOf = new Map((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => [u.id, u.parent ?? null]));
81	  const dropped = [];
82	  const actions = [];
83	
84	  const isUnitAncestorOrSelf = (candidate, id) => {
85	    let cur = candidate;
86	    for (let i = 0; cur != null && i < 1000; i++) {
87	      if (cur === id) return true;
88	      cur = unitParentOf.get(cur) ?? null;
89	    }
90	    return false;
91	  };
92	
93	  const isAncestorOrSelf = (candidate, id) => {
94	    let cur = candidate;
95	    for (let i = 0; cur != null && i < 1000; i++) {
96	      if (cur === id) return true;
97	      cur = parentOf.get(cur) ?? null;
98	    }
99	    return false;
100	  };
101	
102	  const validParent = (id, parent) => parent != null && known.has(parent) && !isAncestorOrSelf(parent, id);
103	
104	  for (const a of Array.isArray(input?.actions) ? input.actions : []) {
105	    const reject = (reason) => dropped.push({ action: a, reason });
106	
107	    // Shape first: op, id and the per-op field whitelist all come from the
108	    // shared schema, so anything past here has the keys it claims to have.
109	    const shape = validateAction(a);
110	    if (!shape.ok) {
111	      reject(shape.errors.join('; '));
112	      continue;
113	    }
114	
115	    const { op, id } = a;
116	    const fields = { ...a.fields };
117	
118	    // Teams the model made up are dropped the same way node ids are, so
119	    // nothing unknown reaches the browser's apply layer.
120	    const badUnitRef = (value) => value != null && !knownUnits.has(value);
121	    const keepKnownDeps = (charter) => {
122	      if (!Array.isArray(charter?.dependsOn)) return charter;
123	      const kept = charter.dependsOn.filter((d) => knownUnits.has(d) && d !== id);
124	      if (kept.length === charter.dependsOn.length) return charter;
125	      reject(`dropped unknown dependsOn entries for ${id}`);
126	      return { ...charter, dependsOn: kept };
127	    };
128	
129	    if (op === 'edit' || op === 'relink') {
130	      if (!known.has(id)) { reject(`unknown id ${id}`); continue; }
131	      if ('parent' in fields && !validParent(id, fields.parent)) {
132	        reject(`bad parent ${fields.parent} for ${id}`);
133	        delete fields.parent;
134	      }
135	      if ('unitId' in fields && badUnitRef(fields.unitId)) {
136	        reject(`unknown team ${fields.unitId} for ${id}`);
137	        delete fields.unitId;
138	      }
139	      // A relink whose only field was the rejected parent has nothing left.
140	      if (!Object.keys(fields).length) { reject('no usable fields'); continue; }
141	      if ('parent' in fields) parentOf.set(id, fields.parent);
142	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
143	    } else if (op === 'add') {
144	      if (known.has(id)) { reject(`add with existing id ${id}`); continue; }
145	      // The model is never allowed to mint a second company root.
146	      if (!fields.level || fields.level === 'company') fields.level = 'kr';
147	      if (!(fields.parent != null && known.has(fields.parent))) { reject(`add with bad parent ${fields.parent}`); continue; }
148	      if ('unitId' in fields && badUnitRef(fields.unitId)) {
149	        reject(`unknown team ${fields.unitId} for ${id}`);
150	        delete fields.unitId;
151	      }
152	      known.add(id);
153	      parentOf.set(id, fields.parent);
154	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
155	    } else if (op === 'editUnit') {
156	      if (!knownUnits.has(id)) { reject(`unknown team ${id}`); continue; }
157	      if ('parent' in fields && fields.parent != null) {
158	        // A team cannot move under itself or under one of its own children.
159	        if (!knownUnits.has(fields.parent) || isUnitAncestorOrSelf(fields.parent, id)) {
160	          reject(`bad parent ${fields.parent} for team ${id}`);
161	          delete fields.parent;
162	        }
163	      }
164	      if ('charter' in fields) fields.charter = keepKnownDeps(fields.charter);
165	      if (!Object.keys(fields).length) { reject('no usable fields'); continue; }
166	      if ('parent' in fields) unitParentOf.set(id, fields.parent ?? null);
167	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
168	    } else if (op === 'addUnit') {
169	      if (knownUnits.has(id)) { reject(`addUnit with existing id ${id}`); continue; }
170	      if (fields.parent != null && !knownUnits.has(fields.parent)) {
171	        reject(`addUnit with bad parent ${fields.parent}`);
172	        fields.parent = null;
173	      }
174	      knownUnits.add(id);
175	      unitParentOf.set(id, fields.parent ?? null);
176	      if ('charter' in fields) fields.charter = keepKnownDeps(fields.charter);
177	      actions.push({ op, id, fields });
178	    } else if (op === 'deleteUnit') {
179	      if (!knownUnits.has(id)) { reject(`unknown team ${id}`); continue; }
180	      // Deleting a team never cascades: its children move up to its parent, so
181	      // only the team itself leaves the known set.
182	      const up = unitParentOf.get(id) ?? null;
183	      for (const [child, parent] of unitParentOf) if (parent === id) unitParentOf.set(child, up);
184	      knownUnits.delete(id);
185	      unitParentOf.delete(id);
186	      actions.push({ op, id });
187	    } else if (op === 'delete') {
188	      if (!known.has(id)) { reject(`unknown id ${id}`); continue; }
189	      const gone = new Set([id]);
190	      let grew = true;
191	      while (grew) {
192	        grew = false;
193	        for (const [child, parent] of parentOf) {
194	          if (gone.has(parent) && !gone.has(child)) { gone.add(child); grew = true; }
195	        }
196	      }
197	      for (const g of gone) { known.delete(g); parentOf.delete(g); }
198	      actions.push({ op, id });
199	    }
200	  }
201	
202	  const highlight = [
203	    ...new Set((Array.isArray(input?.highlight) ? input.highlight : []).filter((id) => typeof id === 'string' && known.has(id)))
204	  ];
205	
206	  const reply =
207	    typeof input?.reply === 'string' && input.reply.trim()
208	      ? input.reply.trim()
209	      : actions.length
210	        ? 'Done.'
211	        : "I couldn't come up with an answer for that — try rephrasing.";
212	
213	  return { reply, actions, highlight, dropped };
214	}

charter: {
  mission:   "why the team exists, one or two sentences",
  process:   "the business process it runs: inputs, steps, outputs, cadence",

```

- `mission` and `process` are prose because personas are prose.
- `owns` is a list because ownership disputes ("who owns activation rate?") are the most
  interesting thing two team agents can argue about, and a list is diffable.
- `dependsOn` is references because reviews ("does Sales' KR depend on something Engineering has
  not committed to?") need to walk a graph, not parse text.

## The four discussion modes (interview answer, 2026-09-11)

All four were chosen. In dependency order:

1. **Chat with one team's agent.** A tab with `mode: 'persona'`, `subject: team`. The system
   prompt is the coach prompt plus "You are speaking as <team>. Here is your charter. Answer as
   this team would, from its priorities and constraints." Cheapest; a direct extension of
   interview tabs.
2. **Agents review each other's OKRs.** Team A's persona is asked to critique Team B's subtree
   for alignment, measurability and unstated dependencies on A. Output is a normal reply +
   highlight, optionally actions. One call per review.
3. **Team-vs-team debate the user moderates.** N personas, one shared transcript, the user picks
   the topic and can interject. Because the service is stateless, the *browser* orchestrates:
   each turn is one `/api/chat` call with `mode: 'persona'`, the speaking team as subject, and
   the shared transcript as history (turns attributed by name in the content). A tab shows the
   transcript with speaker labels.
4. **Agents negotiate and propose tree edits.** Mode 3 with a closing turn: a neutral "coach"
   call that reads the transcript and returns `actions`. Actions go through `commit()` like
   everything else, so the user can undo the whole negotiation in one step.

## Invariants the near-term plan must not break

- **The charter is self-contained.** No field may depend on UI state or on another document.
  A charter pasted into a prompt with the team's subtree must be enough.
- **Team edits are Actions.** Modes 1 to 4 will propose charter changes; they must be undoable
  and land in history like node edits.
- **A team can be handed to the model without its people.** `people` stays optional and out of
  the persona; personas represent teams, not individuals.
- **`owner` never disagrees with `unitId`.** The apply layer derives `owner` from the unit name
  whenever `unitId` changes, so prompts that read `owner` and prompts that read `unitId` agree.

## Alternatives considered

- **Personas as a separate `agents` section in the document.** Rejected: it would drift from the
  team it describes. The charter *is* the persona source; a future `persona` field on the unit
  (tone, red lines) can be added additively if needed.
- **Server-side orchestration of debates** (a `/api/discuss` endpoint that loops). Rejected for
  now: it breaks the stateless invariant and hides turns from the user. Browser-driven turns
  keep each call inspectable and interruptible. Revisit if latency of N sequential calls is
  unacceptable.
- **Free-text `domain` instead of `owns[]`.** Rejected: ownership overlap detection between two
  teams is the first useful agent argument, and it needs discrete items.

## Open questions for the future plan

- Should a debate transcript be exportable into `history`? Probably as a `change` with empty
  actions and the transcript as `reason`, but the 4000-char `reason` cap may be too small.

6. **Teams are data the model can be handed.** A team's charter (mission, process, ownership
   domain, dependencies) is written so it can be dropped into a system prompt verbatim. That is
   the bridge to agents; see the companion doc.

## Vocabulary

- **Document**: `{ schemaVersion, meta, company?, tree, history? }`. What is exported, imported,
  bundled.
- **Tree / Node**: the OKR hierarchy. Flat nodes with `parent` pointers. Levels company →
  objective → kr.
- **Team** (schema name: `CompanyUnit`): an org unit with an optional **charter**. Nodes point at
  a team by `unitId`; `owner` is the display string derived from it.
- **Action**: one edit. Node ops `edit | relink | add | delete`; team ops
  `editUnit | addUnit | deleteUnit`.
- **Commit**: applying a batch of Actions with an actor and a reason. Produces one undo step and
  one history change.
- **Selection**: the node the user clicked. **Highlight**: the nodes the assistant pointed at.
  Selection wins; highlight is transient.
- **Panel**: the one thing open on the left of the scene: a node (read or edit), a team, or the
  team list.
- **Context**: what the user is looking at, sent with a message: selection, panel, focused field,
  highlights, dataset.
- **Tab**: one conversation with a **mode** (`free`, `interview-node`, `interview-team`,
  `interview-new`) and a **subject** (a node, a team, or a parent for a new node).
- **Interview**: a tab where the assistant asks, one question at a time, and ends by proposing
  Actions.
- **Persona** (future): a system prompt built from a team's charter so an agent speaks as that
  team.

## Why these pieces, in this order

```
BUNDLED_DATASETS ─┐
CAMERA_LEVEL ─────┼── independent, ship in any order
CLEAR_HIGHLIGHT ──┘
        │
OKR_NODE_EDITOR ── introduces commit() + history
        │
TEAM_MODEL_AND_EDITOR ── company in state/request, team actions, team editor, team labels
        │
CHAT_CONTEXT ── panel/field/highlight context in the request
        │
CHAT_TABS_AND_INTERVIEWS ── modes, subjects, launch buttons
        │
(future) TEAM_AGENT_DISCUSSIONS ── personas, debates, reviews
```

- **Datasets first** because teams need somewhere to live in data, and because every later
  verification step starts with "load dataset X".
- **Editor before teams** because the editor establishes `commit()` and history, which the team
  editor reuses without inventing a second path.
- **Teams before context** because "the open team editor" is one of the things context reports,
  and the request must already carry `company` for the model to name teams.
- **Context before tabs** because an interview about a team is a tab whose subject is that
  team; the context machinery is what makes the subject resolvable.

## Alternatives considered

- **A `/api/interview` endpoint.** Rejected: interviews are the same tool call with a different
  system prompt; a second endpoint would duplicate validation and drift.
- **Team edits outside the Action system** (a `setCompany()` setter). Rejected: interviews about
  a team must be able to propose team edits, and those must be undoable and recorded. One action
  vocabulary or two of everything.
- **Replacing `owner` with a required team reference** (breaking, `schemaVersion: 2`). Rejected
  for now: additive `unitId` with `owner` as derived display text keeps every existing file and
  prompt valid. Revisit when a migration is worth writing.
- **OrbitControls for the camera.** Rejected: it never rolls, but it also forbids the user from
  rolling. The ask was "level on auto-moves, free on user moves".
- **Persisting tabs or the chosen dataset.** Deferred: nothing persists yet; adding persistence
  for one thing invites a half-built persistence layer.

## Horizons

Recorded 2026-09-11 so near-term decisions keep the doors open. Only Horizon 1 has plans.

| Horizon | What | Why it waits |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Interaction model and value** (now) | The seven plans above: datasets, camera, editor, teams, context, tabs. | Everything later assumes the tree, teams and chat are worth using by one person. |
| **2. Agents that work and measure** (mid) | An agent runs *as a team* to execute one of its OKRs through connected tools (e.g. triage 90% of incoming issues on a GitHub repo and rank them by priority). Agents and users both record progress. A progress dashboard reads it. Designed in [Agents as Executors - Design](Agents%20as%20Executors%20-%20Design.md). | Needs a team charter that is real (Horizon 1), a place to run long jobs, and tool connections with credentials. |
| **3. Shared, live document** (distant) | The document lives in a realtime JSON-document database so several team members edit and chat against it at once. | Needs the interaction model settled first; a multi-user store hardens whatever shape it is given. |

Seams to keep open now, because they are cheap today and expensive later:

- **The document is the unit of truth** (invariant 4). A JSON-document realtime store
  (Firestore, Yjs/Automerge, RxDB) can hold an `OkrDocument` as-is; nothing in the app addresses
  state by anything other than the document and the ids inside it.

  font-size: 11px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;

}

.detail ul.checks li { display: block; }

/* the legend is pointer-events: none, so its one control opts back in */
.legend .toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; cursor: pointer; pointer-events: auto; }
.legend .toggle input { margin: 0; accent-color: var(--accent); }

.topbar button.on { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }

.bar .good, .pct.good { background: var(--good); }

.pct { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; color: #0b0f17; border-radius: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; white-space: nowrap; }

/* ── chat ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

}

.chip { text-align: left; border-radius: 10px; padding: 8px 12px; background: var(--panel-2); color: var(--text); }

.msg.user .bubble { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }
.msg.error .bubble { border-color: var(--bad); color: var(--bad); }

// Every fixture under test/fixtures/ is a self-describing case:
//
//   { "schema": "okr-tree", "data": … }            must validate
//   { "schema": "okr-tree", "at": "/nodes", "data": … }  must fail, with an
//                                                        error on that path
//
// Adding a case is adding a file. `at: ""` means "fail anywhere", for the
// whole-object failures (a missing required property reports on the parent).

import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

import {
  validateAction,
  validateChatRequest,
  validateChatResponse,
  validateCompany,
  validateHistory,
  validateOkrDocument,
  validateOkrNode,
  validateOkrTree
} from '../index.js';

const BY_NAME = {
  action: validateAction,
  'chat-request': validateChatRequest,
  'chat-response': validateChatResponse,
  company: validateCompany,
  history: validateHistory,
  'okr-document': validateOkrDocument,
  'okr-node': validateOkrNode,
  'okr-tree': validateOkrTree
};

const FIXTURES = fileURLToPath(new URL('./fixtures/', import.meta.url));
const load = (kind) =>
  readdirSync(join(FIXTURES, kind))
    .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))
    .sort()
    .map((f) => [f, JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(FIXTURES, kind, f), 'utf8'))]);

test('every fixture names a schema this package validates', () => {
  for (const kind of ['valid', 'invalid']) {
    for (const [name, fx] of load(kind)) {
      assert.ok(BY_NAME[fx.schema], `${kind}/${name} names unknown schema "${fx.schema}"`);
    }
  }
});

test('valid fixtures validate', async (t) => {
  const fixtures = load('valid');
  assert.ok(fixtures.length >= 10, 'expected a meaningful number of valid fixtures');
  for (const [name, fx] of fixtures) {
    await t.test(name, () => {
      const out = BY_NAME[fx.schema](fx.data);
      assert.ok(out.ok, `expected ${name} to validate, got:\n  ${out.errors?.join('\n  ')}`);
    });
  }
});

test('invalid fixtures fail on the path they name', async (t) => {
  const fixtures = load('invalid');
  assert.ok(fixtures.length >= 10, 'expected a meaningful number of invalid fixtures');
  for (const [name, fx] of fixtures) {
    await t.test(name, () => {
      const out = BY_NAME[fx.schema](fx.data);
      assert.equal(out.ok, false, `expected ${name} to fail validation`);
      assert.ok(out.errors.length, 'a failure must come with at least one error');
      for (const e of out.errors) assert.match(e, /^\S*: /, `error is not "path: message": ${e}`);
      if (fx.at) {
        assert.ok(
          out.errors.some((e) => e.startsWith(`${fx.at}:`)),
          `expected an error on "${fx.at}", got:\n  ${out.errors.join('\n  ')}`
        );
      }
    });
  }
});

test('errors never leak raw Ajv objects', () => {
  const out = validateOkrTree({ nodes: [{ id: 1 }] });
  assert.equal(out.ok, false);
  for (const e of out.errors) assert.equal(typeof e, 'string');
});

// Builds schema/dist/ from schema/src/. Six steps, each loud on failure:
//
//   1. meta-validate every src/*.schema.json against draft-07
//   2. generate dist/types.d.ts with the json-schema-to-typescript fork
//   3. precompile Ajv validators into dist/validators.js (+ .d.ts)
//   4. copy the raw schemas into dist/json/
//   5. flatten chat-response into dist/json/tool/respond-input.json for Claude
//   6. tsc --noEmit over the generated types
//
// Run it as `npm run build:schema` from the repo root.

import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import Ajv from 'ajv';
import addFormats from 'ajv-formats';
import standaloneCode from 'ajv/dist/standalone/index.js';
import { compileFromFile } from 'json-schema-to-typescript';
import $RefParser from '@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser';

const PKG = join(HERE, '..');
const SRC = join(PKG, 'src');
const DIST = join(PKG, 'dist');

const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(PKG, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
const step = (n, what) => console.log(`[schema] ${n}/6 ${what}`);
const fail = (msg) => {
  console.error(`[schema] BUILD FAILED: ${msg}`);
  process.exit(1);
};

// Keys must match the exports listed in index.js and dist/validators.d.ts.
//
// The seven *Action entries compile a single oneOf branch each. Ajv reports a
// oneOf failure as every branch's complaints at once, with no way to tell which
// branch an error came from — resolving a $ref rewrites schemaPath relative to
// the target. Validating the branch the `op` names gives a usable message.
const VALIDATORS = {
  validateOkrDocument: 'okr-document.schema.json',
  validateOkrTree: 'okr-tree.schema.json',
  validateOkrNode: 'o

... [3852 characters truncated] ...

ompilation failed: ${err.message}`);
}

// Ajv's esm output uses `export` for the validators but still reaches for its
// own runtime helpers with `require()`, which throws in an ES module and would
// not survive bundling either. Hoist each one into a real default import; for
// these CJS modules that binding is module.exports, so the `.default` and
// `.fullFormats` lookups after it still resolve.
// The specifiers are deep paths into CJS packages ("ajv/dist/runtime/ucs2length"),
// which require() resolves extensionlessly but ESM does not.
const required = [...new Set([...validators.matchAll(/require\("([^"]+)"\)/g)].map((m) => m[1]))];
const imports = required.map(
  (mod, i) => `import __dep${i} from ${JSON.stringify(/\.[a-z]+$/.test(mod) ? mod : `${mod}.js`)};`
);
for (const [i, mod] of required.entries()) {
  validators = validators.split(`require(${JSON.stringify(mod)})`).join(`__dep${i}`);
}
if (/\brequire\s*\(/.test(validators)) fail('validators.js still calls require() after the ESM rewrite');

writeFileSync(
  join(DIST, 'validators.js'),
  `/* Generated by schema/scripts/build.mjs. DO NOT EDIT. */\n${imports.join('\n')}\n${validators}`
);
if (required.length) console.log(`[schema]     hoisted ${required.length} Ajv runtime require() calls to imports`);

const validatorTypes = `/* Generated by schema/scripts/build.mjs. DO NOT EDIT. */
/** An Ajv precompiled validator: returns true/false and parks failures on \`.errors\`. */
export interface CompiledValidator {
  (data: unknown): boolean;
  errors?: null | { instancePath: string; schemaPath: string; keyword: string; message?: string; params: Record<string, unknown> }[];
}
${Object.keys(VALIDATORS)
  .map((name) => `export declare const ${name}: CompiledValidator;`)
  .join('\n')}
`;
writeFileSync(join(DIST, 'validators.d.ts'), validatorTypes);

// ── 4. raw schema copies ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step(4, `copying ${files.length} schemas to dist/json/`);
for (const [f, schema] of schemas) {
  writeFileSync(join(DIST, 'json', f), JSON.stringify(schema, null, 2) + '\n');
}

// ── 5. flattened tool schema ────────────────────────────────────────────────
step(5, 'flattening dist/json/tool/respond-input.json');

// Claude's `input_schema` cannot follow external $refs, so the tool gets a
// fully dereferenced copy. Descriptions carry over from src/, which is why
// every property in the schemas is written for the model as well as for us.
// Dereferencing splices whole files in, so the inlined copies bring their own
// $schema/$id and their now-unreachable definitions with them. Strip those
// everywhere, not just at the root.
const DROP = new Set(['$schema', '$id', '$comment', 'definitions']);
const prune = (node, seen = new Map()) => {
  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map((v) => prune(v, seen));
  if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return node;
  if (seen.has(node)) return seen.get(node);
  const out = {};
  seen.set(node, out);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(node)) if (!DROP.has(k)) out[k] = prune(v, seen);
  return out;
};

const tool = prune(await $RefParser.dereference(join(SRC, 'chat-response.schema.json')));
tool.required = ['reply', 'actions', 'highlight'];

const leftover = JSON.stringify(tool).match(/"\$(ref|id|schema)"/g);
if (leftover) fail(`respond-input.json still contains ${leftover.join(', ')} after dereferencing`);

writeFileSync(join(DIST, 'json', 'tool', 'respond-input.json'), JSON.stringify(tool, null, 2) + '\n');

// index.js is bundled for the browser as well as loaded by the service, so it
// cannot read package.json off disk or use a JSON import attribute. Bake both
// into a plain ESM module instead.
writeFileSync(
  join(DIST, 'meta.js'),
  `/* Generated by schema/scripts/build.mjs. DO NOT EDIT. */
export const PACKAGE_VERSION = ${JSON.stringify(pkg.version)};
export const RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA = ${JSON.stringify(tool, null, 2)};
`
);
writeFileSync(
  join(DIST, 'meta.d.ts'),
  `/* Generated by schema/scripts/build.mjs. DO NOT EDIT. */
export declare const PACKAGE_VERSION: string;
export declare const RESPOND_INPUT_SCHEMA: Record<string, unknown>;
`
);

// ── 6. type-check ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
step(6, 'type-checking generated declarations');

// npm hoists devDeps to the workspace root, so resolve tsc rather than
// assuming it sits in schema/node_modules.
const tsc = createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('typescript/bin/tsc');
try {
  // tsconfig.check.json rather than CLI flags: it pins lib/moduleResolution and
  // sets `types: []`, so the check sees our declarations and nothing a hoisted
  // @types/* package happens to drag in.
  execFileSync(process.execPath, [tsc, '-p', 'tsconfig.check.json'], { cwd: PKG, stdio: 'pipe', encoding: 'utf8' });
} catch (err) {
  fail(`tsc rejected the generated declarations:\n${err.stdout ?? ''}${err.stderr ?? ''}`);
}

console.log(`[schema] built ${pkg.name}@${pkg.version} → dist/`);

  const types = read('../dist/types.d.ts');
  for (const name of ['OkrNode', 'OkrTree', 'OkrDocument', 'Company', 'TeamCharter', 'History', 'ChatRequest', 'ChatResponse']) {
    const count = types.match(new RegExp(`^export interface ${name} \\{`, 'gm'))?.length ?? 0;

  }
});

});

// The bundled OkrDocuments the app can boot from.
//
// Every dataset is a file in ../assets/datasets/*.json in exactly the format
// Export writes and Import reads, so a bundled tree and a downloaded one are
// interchangeable — and `company` / `history` can be added to a dataset later
// without inventing a second format.
//
// Vite inlines the JSON at build time (eager glob), so there is no fetch, no
// loading state and no 404 path: if a file is here, it is in the bundle.

import manifest from '../assets/datasets/manifest.json';
import { parseDocument } from '@okr-viewer/schema';

const files = import.meta.glob('../assets/datasets/*.json', { eager: true, import: 'default' });

const slugOf = (path) => path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1, -'.json'.length);

const documents = new Map();
for (const [path, document] of Object.entries(files)) {
  const slug = slugOf(path);
  if (slug === 'manifest') continue;
  documents.set(slug, document);
}

// Manifest order first, then anything it does not mention, alphabetically — so
// dropping a new file into the folder works without touching the manifest.
const ordered = [
  ...(manifest.order ?? []).filter((id) => documents.has(id)),
  ...[...documents.keys()].filter((id) => !(manifest.order ?? []).includes(id)).sort()
];

/** @type {{ id: string, title: string, document: object }[]} */
export const DATASETS = ordered.map((id) => ({
  id,
  title: documents.get(id).meta?.title || id,
  document: documents.get(id)
}));

if (!documents.has(manifest.default)) {
  // A blank page with a stack trace beats a silent fallback to whichever file
  // happened to sort first.
  throw new Error(
    `[datasets] manifest.default "${manifest.default}" names no file; have: ${[...documents.keys()].join(', ')}`
  );
}

/** Slug of the dataset the app boots with. */
export const DEFAULT_DATASET_ID = manifest.default;

/** @returns {{ id: string, title: string, document: object }} the dataset, or the default if `id` is unknown. */
export function getDataset(id) {
  return DATASETS.find((d) => d.id === id) ?? DATASETS.find((d) => d.id === DEFAULT_DATASET_ID);
}

// A bad hand edit to a dataset should fail loudly at boot, not halfway through
// a demo. Dev only: dead code in the production bundle.
if (import.meta.env.DEV) {
  for (const { id, document } of DATASETS) {

// The interview rules, shared by all three interview modes. They are the whole
// difference between a coach who answers and one who asks: without the "one
// question per turn" clamp the model writes the entire interview in one reply
// and then answers it itself.
const INTERVIEW_RULES = `Rules for this interview, and they override the conversational defaults above:
- Ask exactly one question per turn. Never two, never a list of them.
- Before each question after the first, reflect what you just heard back in one sentence, so the user can correct you.
- Ask at most eight questions. Fewer is better: stop as soon as you could write the answer yourself.
- Keep sending an empty \`actions\` array while you are still asking. Only the closing turn carries actions.
- When you have enough — or the moment the user says they are done — stop asking, summarise what you heard in \`reply\`, and return the actions that write it into the document.
- \`highlight\` what this interview is about on every single turn, so the user can see it while they answer.
- "Begin the interview." is the app opening the tab, not something the user typed. Do not acknowledge it or say you are starting; just ask your first question.`;

// What this tab is for, in the shape the mode calls for. `subject` has already
// been checked against this document by the service, so every id below
// resolves; an unknown one arrives here as mode `free` instead.
function roleBlock(tree, company, mode, subject) {
  if (!mode || mode === 'free') return '';

  const nodes = new Map(tree.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
  const units = new Map((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => [u.id, u]));
  const label = (id) => nodes.get(id)?.label ?? id;

  if (mode === 'interview-node' && subject?.kind === 'node') {
    const node = nodes.get(subject.id);
    const team = node.unitId && units.get(node.unitId) ? `, owned by ${units.get(node.unitId).name}` : '';
    const supports = node.parent ? ` and confirm it really supports "${label(node.parent)}"` : '';
    const has = [
      node.metric ? `its metric is "${node.metric}"` : 'it has no metric',
      node.target ? `its target is "${node.target}"` : 'it has no target'
    ].join(' and ');
    return `
## Your role in this conversation
You are interviewing the user about "${node.label}" (${node.level}${team}, id \`${node.id}\`). Right now ${has}.

Your goal: turn it into an outcome with a metric and a target${supports}. Ask about the work behind it — what would actually be different if it succeeded, what number would move, where that number is today, and where it needs to be. Do not propose the wording yourself until the closing turn.

${INTERVIEW_RULES}
- Close with an \`edit\` on \`${node.id}\` carrying the label, metric, target and \`contributes\` you arrived at. Never invent numbers the user did not give you: if they do not know the baseline, ask for a way to find it, and leave that part of the target as the thing to measure.
`;

      `owns: ${charter.owns?.length ? JSON.stringify(charter.owns) : 'EMPTY'}`,
      `dependsOn: ${charter.dependsOn?.length ? charter.dependsOn.map((d) => units.get(d)?.name ?? d).join(', ') : 'EMPTY'}`

## Your role in this conversation
You are interviewing the user about the ${unit.name} team (id \`${unit.id}\`). Its charter as written today:

<charter>
${written}
</charter>

It owns ${owned.length} node${owned.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} in the tree${owned.length ? `: ${owned.map((n) => `"${n.label}"`).join(', ')}` : ''}.

Your goal: fill or sharpen that charter — why the team exists, the process it runs (inputs, steps, outputs, cadence), what it is the accountable owner of, and whose output it needs — and check that its objectives fit what it actually does. Ask about what is EMPTY or vague above; never ask the user to tell you something the charter already says.

${INTERVIEW_RULES}
- Close with an \`editUnit\` on \`${unit.id}\` carrying only the charter fields you learned about, plus node \`edit\`s if the interview showed one of its objectives is wrong.

${

    : `You are helping the user define a new OKR, and nothing has been decided yet — not even where it goes. Your FIRST question is which objective in the tree it supports (or whether it is a new objective under the company root). Everything else comes after that.`
}

Your goal: one node that states an outcome, with a metric and a target, and a \`contributes\` score that honestly says how well it supports its parent. Ask what would be different if it worked, what number says so, and where that number stands today.

${INTERVIEW_RULES}
- Close with an \`add\` action. Its id must be new and of the form "kr-<short-slug>" or "obj-<short-slug>", and its \`parent\` must be ${parent ? `\`${parent.id}\`` : 'the node the user named in their first answer'}.
`;

export function validateResponse(tree, company, input) {
+
// What the tab says it is about, checked against the document it came with.
//
// Same spirit as sanitizeContext: a subject that names nothing is a tab whose
// subject has been deleted, imported away or switched out from under it, and
// that is never worth a 400 on a message the user has already typed. The mode
// falls back to `free` and the reason is reported so it can be logged — a
// client that keeps sending subjects this tree does not have is a bug worth
// seeing.
//
// `interview-new` is the one case that survives a bad reference: a parent that
// is gone leaves a perfectly good interview about a node that does not exist
// yet, so only the parent is dropped and the model asks which objective it
// supports instead.
export function resolveTab(tree, company, mode, subject) {
  const free = (dropped = null) => ({ mode: 'free', subject: null, dropped });
  if (!mode || mode === 'free') return free();

  const known = new Set(tree.nodes.map((n) => n.id));
  const knownUnits = new Set((Array.isArray(company?.units) ? company.units : []).map((u) => u.id));

  if (mode === 'interview-node') {
    if (subject?.kind !== 'node') return free('no node subject — falling back to free');
    if (!known.has(subject.id)) return free(`node ${subject.id} is not in this tree — falling back to free`);
    return { mode, subject: { kind: 'node', id: subject.id }, dropped: null };
  }

  if (mode === 'interview-team') {
    if (subject?.kind !== 'team') return free('no team subject — falling back to free');
    if (!knownUnits.has(subject.id)) return free(`team ${subject.id} is not in this org — falling back to free`);
    return { mode, subject: { kind: 'team', id: subject.id }, dropped: null };
  }

  if (mode === 'interview-new') {
    if (subject?.kind !== 'new') return free('no new-node subject — falling back to free');
    const parentId = subject.parentId ?? null;
    if (parentId != null && !known.has(parentId)) {
      return {
        mode,
        subject: { kind: 'new', parentId: null },
        dropped: `parent ${parentId} is not in this tree — asking for one instead`
      };
    }
    return { mode, subject: { kind: 'new', parentId }, dropped: null };
  }

  return free(`unknown mode ${mode} — falling back to free`);
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Post one turn to the local service, the way the browser would.

  ask.py <state.json>

state.json: { "mode":…, "subject":…, "selectedNodeId":…, "context":…,
              "history":[…], "message":"…", "dataset":"workflow-platform-fy26" }

Prints the reply, appends the turn to history, and writes state.json back, so
a multi-turn interview is a sequence of runs against the same file.
"""
import json, sys, urllib.request

ROOT = "/Users/tmiv74/OKR-Display"
state_path = sys.argv[1]
state = json.load(open(state_path))
doc = json.load(open(f"{ROOT}/web/src/assets/datasets/{state.get('dataset','workflow-platform-fy26')}.json"))

if len(sys.argv) > 2:
    state["message"] = sys.argv[2]

body = {
    "tree": doc["tree"],
    "company": doc.get("company"),
    "message": state["message"],
    "history": state.get("history", []),
}
for k in ("selectedNodeId", "context", "mode", "subject"):
    if k in state:
        body[k] = state[k]

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://localhost:8787/api/chat",
    data=json.dumps(body).encode(),

<script>
  let {
    chats = [],
    activeChatId = null,
    onSelectChat,
    onCloseChat,
    onNewChat,
    onSend,
    onRecall,
    onUndo,
    canUndo = false
  } = $props();

  const active = $derived(chats.find((c) => c.id === activeChatId) ?? chats[0] ?? null);
  const messages = $derived(active?.messages ?? []);
  const loading = $derived(active?.loading ?? false);
  const isInterview = $derived(!!active && active.mode !== 'free');

  // One composer element, one draft per tab. The element stays put across a tab
  // switch on purpose: it is inside `.chat`, which is how App decides that
  // leaving a field for the chat box holds that field — tearing it down and
  // rebuilding it would drop focus mid-thought.
  let drafts = $state({});
  const draft = $derived(drafts[activeChatId] ?? '');

  let listEl;
  let menuOpen = $state(false);

  const suggestions = [
    'Which key results don’t clearly support a company objective?',
    'Rewrite those so they’re measurable and tie them to the right objective.',
    'Which team is carrying the most risk?'
  ];

  // A title long enough to need it is cut here rather than in CSS, so the tab
  // keeps its shape and the full title is still there on hover.
  const short = (t) => (t.length > 24 ? `${t.slice(0, 23)}…` : t);

  $effect(() => {
    void activeChatId;
    void messages.length;
    void loading;
    requestAnimationFrame(() => listEl?.scrollTo({ top: listEl.scrollHeight, behavior: 'smooth' }));
  });

  function submit(e) {
    e?.preventDefault();
    const m = draft.trim();
    if (!m || loading || !active) return;
    drafts[active.id] = '';
    onSend(active.id, m);
  }

  function onKey(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) submit(e);
  }

  function open(options) {
    menuOpen = false;
    onNewChat(options);
  }
</script>

<svelte:window onclick={() => (menuOpen = false)} />

<aside class="chat">
  <div class="tabs">
    {#each chats as c (c.id)}
      <div class="tab" class:on={c.id === activeChatId} class:busy={c.loading}>
        <button class="name" title={c.title} onclick={() => onSelectChat(c.id)}>{short(c.title)}</button>
        {#if chats.length > 1}
          <button class="close" aria-label="Close {c.title}" onclick={() => onCloseChat(c.id)}>×</button>
        {/if}
      </div>
    {/each}
    <div class="new">
      <button class="plus" aria-label="New conversation" onclick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); menuOpen = !menuOpen; }}>+</button>
      {#if menuOpen}
        <!-- svelte-ignore a11y_no_static_element_interactions -->
        <div class="menu" onclick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>
          <button onclick={() => open({ mode: 'free' })}>New chat</button>
          <button onclick={() => open({ mode: 'interview-new' })}>Interview me about a new OKR</button>
        </div>
      {/if}
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="messages" bind:this={listEl}>
    {#if !messages.length && !loading}
      <div class="empty">
        {#if isInterview}
          <p>The assistant asks, you answer. Say “that’s enough” to wrap up.</p>
        {:else}
          <p>Ask the tree anything, or tell it what to change.</p>
          {#each suggestions as s}
            <button class="chip" onclick={() => onSend(active.id, s)} disabled={loading}>{s}</button>
          {/each}
        {/if}
      </div>
    {/if}
    {#if isInterview && loading && !messages.some((m) => m.role === 'assistant')}
      <p class="hint">The assistant asks, you answer. Say “that’s enough” to wrap up.</p>
    {/if}
    {#each messages as m}
      {#if !m.hidden}
        <div class="msg {m.role}" class:error={m.error} class:note={m.note}>
          <div class="bubble">{m.content}</div>
          {#if m.role === 'assistant' && (m.highlight?.length || m.actions)}
            <div class="meta">
              {#if m.actions}
                <span class="pill edit">{m.actions} edit{m.actions === 1 ? '' : 's'}</span>
                {#if isInterview}
                  <!-- an interview ends in a commit, so the way back out is
                       right where it landed rather than up in the toolbar -->
                  <button class="pill" onclick={onUndo} disabled={!canUndo}>Undo</button>
                {/if}
              {/if}
              {#if m.highlight?.length}
                <button class="pill" onclick={() => onRecall(m.highlight)}>
                  show {m.highlight.length} node{m.highlight.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}
                </button>
              {/if}
            </div>
          {/if}
        </div>
      {/if}
    {/each}
    {#if loading}
      <div class="msg assistant"><div class="bubble thinking"><span></span><span></span><span></span></div></div>
    {/if}
  </div>
  <form onsubmit={submit}>
    <textarea
      value={draft}
      oninput={(e) => (drafts[activeChatId] = e.currentTarget.value)}
      onkeydown={onKey}
      rows="2"
      placeholder={isInterview ? 'Answer, or say “that’s enough”…' : 'Ask about the tree, or tell me what to change…'}
      disabled={loading}
    ></textarea>
    <button type="submit" disabled={loading || !draft.trim()}>Send</button>
  </form>
</aside>

.tabs {

  overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.tabs::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
.tab {
  display: flex; align-items: center; flex: none;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-bottom: 0;
  border-radius: 8px 8px 0 0;
  background: var(--panel-2);
  margin-bottom: -1px;
}
.tab .name {
  background: none; border: 0; padding: 5px 4px 5px 10px;
  color: var(--muted); font-size: 12px; white-space: nowrap;
}

.tab .close:hover { color: var(--text); }
.tab.on { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--panel); }
.tab.on .name { color: var(--accent); }
/* a tab whose request is still out says so without stealing the transcript */
.tab.busy .name::after { content: ' ·'; animation: blink 1.2s infinite; }
.new { position: relative; flex: none; display: flex; align-items: center; }
.new .plus { background: none; border: 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 16px; line-height: 1; padding: 2px 8px; }

.messages { flex: 1; overflow: auto; padding: 16px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }

# Plan: Send the user's view context with every message so the assistant resolves references

Concept: [OKR Viewer - Product Vision](../../Concepts/OKR%20Viewer%20-%20Product%20Vision.md)
("pointing plus seeing").
...
  set and nothing else. That is coaching behaviour, not a context failure — but a stricter reading
  of this plan's second verification bullet needs the extra turn.
- *Highlights can be a justified superset.* "What does this team own?" on Marketing highlights
  Marketing's four nodes plus the two owned by Content and Field Marketing, which roll up under
  Marketing, and the reply says so. The bullet asked for equality; the model's answer is better
  than the bullet.
- *A node panel with no selection drops.* `sanitizeContext` requires an id for `kind: 'node'`, so
  a node panel that somehow has no selected node is dropped whole and logged. That combination
  should not occur — `select()` only opens a node panel for a real id — but it is a log line to
  recognise rather than a puzzle.

### Verification transcript

Run against `workflow-platform-fy26` and the live service (real model replies, `claude-sonnet-5`):

|---|---|
| `kr-7` selected, edit mode, cursor in `metric`, "what should this be?" | proposes a metric for that KR, `highlight: [kr-7]`, no actions. `ctx=node:kr-7/metric` |
| "which key results are weak?" then "move those under Sales" | names back exactly the five pulsing KRs and asks to confirm; on "yes, all of them" emits `relink` for exactly `kr-4, kr-7, kr-9, kr-13, kr-21`, all to `obj-3` |
| Marketing's charter open, "what does this team own?" | answers from the charter and the tree, highlights Marketing's nodes plus its sub-teams' two, no "which team?" |
| Teams list open, nothing selected, "who owns the most KRs?" | answered from `company` by `unitId`, guesses at no panel |
| `context.panel.id = "no-such-team"`, `highlighted: ["kr-5", "ghost-1"]` | 200; `[chat] context: dropped ["panel team:no-such-team","highlighted ghost-1"]`, `ctx=none` |
| `npm run test:schema` | 115 pass, including the two new fixtures |
| Browser, Marketing charter, cursor in Mission, "what should this say?" | request carries `{"panel":{"kind":"team","id":"marketing","field":"mission"},…}`; reply is about Marketing's mission. `ctx=team:marketing/mission` |
| Browser, `kr-7` in edit mode, cursor in `metric`, message typed over several seconds | request carries `{"panel":{"kind":"node","id":"kr-7","editing":true,"field":"metric"},…}` |

## Completion notes

- **Planned vs. actual.** All six phases landed as written, and the shape held: `mode` + `subject`
  on the request, one `send(chatId, …)`, one `## Your role in this conversation` section in
  `service/prompt.js`, launchers in both editors and in the `+` menu. Nothing about the response
  needed to change — an interview closes by returning `actions`, which go through `commit()` like
  any other edit, so undo and history came free. The file:line citations had all drifted (this
  plan was written before its predecessors landed on `main`); the code they named was still where
  the plan said it was, one function down.
- **Mid-flight adjustments.**
  - *`context` is a sibling, not a replacement.* CHAT_CONTEXT shipped between the writing and the
    doing, so the request now carries `context` **and** `mode`/`subject`. They answer different
    questions — what the user is looking at versus what this tab is for — and `roleBlock()` sits
    directly above `viewBlock()` so the view block stays last, which is where it has to be.
  - *The service had its own history cap.* The plan's risk section raised the browser's ten-turn
    slice to 24 for interview tabs but missed `sanitizeHistory(history, maxTurns = 12)` in
    `service/validate.js`, which would have re-truncated it. Both caps are now mode-dependent.
  - *`interview-new` survives a stale parent.* Phase 5 says an unknown subject downgrades to
    `free`. For `interview-new` that throws away a perfectly good interview, so a `parentId` this
    tree does not have is dropped on its own and the interview simply asks which objective it
    supports. `interview-node` and `interview-team` downgrade as planned.
  - *`resolveTab()` lives in `service/validate.js`*, beside `sanitizeContext()` — it is the same
    kind of thing (a reference check against the document that never 400s), and `index.js` stays a
    route.
  - *The `+` popover moved out of the scrolling strip.* `overflow-x: auto` on the tab row clips
    absolutely positioned children vertically too, so the menu was invisible. `.tabs` is now a
    plain flex row holding a scrolling `.strip` and the `+`.
  - *Launch buttons sit directly under the panel header*, not inside it: the header row is a level
    badge and Edit/Close, and a third element wrapped badly at 320px.
  - *App notes land in the active tab.* Undo, import, export and dataset switches write their one
    line into whichever conversation the user is looking at.
- **Surprises / residual risks.**
  - *The kick-off turn never leaked.* Across four interviews no reply began with "Sure, I'll begin
    the interview" — the prompt line that calls the phrase an app signal seems to be enough. The
    risk is still real if the rules move earlier in the prompt.
  - *Prompt ordering held.* The role block above the view block, the view block last: interviews
    resolved their subject and the free tab's "what should this be?" still answers about the
    focused field. No reordering was needed.
  - *One verification bullet is unreachable.* Phase 3.2 hides the `×` on the only tab, so
    `closeChat()`'s "closing the last tab yields a fresh Chat" branch cannot be triggered from the
    UI. The code keeps it as a guard; the bullet is dead as written.
  - *Tabs are in memory only* (Decision 6), so a reload loses an interview mid-flight. That is the
    same deal every other piece of state has today, and it will stop being acceptable at the same
    moment.
  - *`node --watch` stopped picking up `service/` edits* across the Docker bind mount during this
    work — the first `build:schema` removed `dist/` under it and it never recovered. Restarting it
    with the same invocation fixed it; a reply with an identical input-token count is the tell.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Add chat tabs with a mode and a subject, and interview launchers

The chat panel becomes a set of tabs. Each tab is a conversation with a
mode (free, interview-node, interview-team, interview-new) and a subject,
and the interview modes invert the coach: the assistant asks one question
per turn and ends by proposing Actions, which go through commit() like any
other edit, so an interview is undoable in one step.

- schema: chat-request gains `mode` and `subject`, with ChatMode /
  ChatSubject types and three fixtures.
- web: `chats` + `activeChatId` replace `messages` / `loading`;
  `send(chatId, message, { hidden })` lands each reply in the tab that
  sent it, so two requests can be in flight at once. Opening an interview
  tab sends a hidden "Begin the interview." turn. Undo, selection and the
  highlight stay global: there is one scene.
- launchers: "Interview me about this OKR" in Detail (plus a new-KR
  variant while editing an objective), "Interview me about this team" in
  TeamEditor, and "Interview me about a new OKR" in the tab bar's + menu.
- service: `resolveTab()` checks the subject against the document and
  downgrades an unknown one to `free` rather than 400-ing; `roleBlock()`
  adds a per-mode "Your role in this conversation" section directly above
  the view block, which stays last. Interview history keeps 24 turns
  rather than 12, on both sides.

Verified in the browser against the live service: a five-question
interview rewrote kr-7 into a measurable KR and Undo reverted it, a team
interview rewrote Marketing's process and owns, and a free tab's messages
were untouched throughout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

A: If this goal succeeded, what would actually look different on social media — more followers, more engagement, more traffic driven to the site, something else? U: Honestly the only thing we care about is traffic that turns into pipeline. Followers are vanity. Social should send people to the site who then book a demo. A: Got it — so the real outcome is demo bookings (or at least site visits) driven by social, not follower counts. Do you already track how many demo bookings or leads come from social channels, and roughly how many is that today? U: Yes, HubSpot attributes it. Social sourced 24 demo bookings last quarter out of about 600 total. A: So today social sources about 24 demo bookings a quarter, roughly 4% of the 600 total. What would a meaningful win look like — a target number or share of demo bookings you'd want social to source by when? U: Doubling it by the end of Q4 feels right - 24 to 50 a quarter. And these should be mid-market, not tiny companies. A: Just to confirm before I close this out: the goal is to raise social-sourced, mid-market demo bookings from 24 to 50 per quarter by end of Q4 — is that the final number and timing you want locked in? U: Yes, that's it. That's enough - write it up. A: Locking it in: "Improve our social media presence" becomes "Grow social-sourced mid-market demo bookings from 24 to 50 per quarter," with a target of 24 → 50 by end of Q4, measured via HubSpot attribution filtered to mid-market accounts. Since this now ties directly to qualified pipeline, I've raised its contribution score to reflect that it genuinely supports the parent goal. — 1 edit · Undo · show 2 nodes

kr-7 afterwards: metric "HubSpot-attributed demo bookings from social channels, mid-market accounts only", target "24 → 50 per quarter by Q4", fit 20% → 75%, weak links 5 → 4. The Undo pill reverted all of it; the free tab's two messages were untouched.

  • Service-side history cap — the plan's risk section raised only the browser's 10-turn slice. sanitizeHistory(history, maxTurns = 12) would have re-truncated it, so both caps are now mode-dependent (10/12 free, 24/24 interview).

  • The + popover had to move out of the scrolling tab strip — overflow-x: auto clips absolutely positioned children vertically; it was invisible until I split .tabs into .tabs + .strip.

  • One verification bullet is unreachable: Phase 3.2 hides the × when only one tab exists, so closeChat()'s "closing the last tab yields a fresh Chat" branch cannot be triggered from the UI. I kept both as the plan specifies and verified the × disappears at one tab; the fallback stays as a guard.
  • Prompt ordering held. roleBlock() sits directly above viewBlock(), view block last. No reordering was needed, and no reply ever acknowledged the "Begin the interview." signal.

I restarted it with the identical invocation (docker exec -d -w /src/service dev sh -c 'node --watch index.js >> /tmp/svc.log 2>&1'); it has picked up every service/ edit since, confirmed by changing input-token counts and the new mode= log field.
